moves we keep in our prayers this week fr patsy mulholland who is moving from our neighbouring parish of loughguile to antrim as part of the annual clergy appointments. we also welcome canon colm mcbride who comes to loughguile. may god bless them and all the priests taking up new appointments in our diocese this week.parish of ballymoney& derrykeighancauseway family of parishes16th august 2026 twentieth sunday of ordinary timegreat faith, no boundaries today's gospel ﬁnds jesus seemingly reluctant to help a canaanite woman pleading for her daughter, telling her it wouldn't be right to give "the children's bread" to "the dogs." it's very strange - until we see what the lord is really doing. he's teaching his apostles, who had brushed the woman aside as a foreign outsider. through their back-and-forth, jesus reveals her deep faith and heals her daughter, showing the twelve that god's love has no borders of race or nation.it's a lesson for us too. as isaiah foretold, god's house is "a house of prayer for all peoples." we're called to carry that welcome beyond our church doors — meeting everyone with respect, and speaking up against the prejudice and division still so present in our world.

549.hymns for mass christ be beside me, christ be before me, christ be behind me, king of my heart. christ be within me, christ be below me, christ be above me, never to part. christ on my right hand, christ on my left hand, christ all around me, shield in the strife. christ in my sleeping, christ in my sitting, christ in my rising, light of my life. christ be in all hearts thinking about me, christ be on all tongues telling of me. christ be the vision in eyes that see me, in ears that hear me, christ ever be.praise, my soul, the king of heaven; to his feet thy tribute bring. ransomed, healed, restored, forgiven, who like me his praise should sing? praise him, praise him, praise him, praise him, praise the everlasting king.praise him for his grace and favour to our fathers in distress. praise him still the same forever, slow to chide, and swift to bless. praise him, praise him, praise him, praise him, glorious in his faithfulness.

4.30pm. to keep in touch with our offers and to see pictures of our stock don’t forget our facebook page @oldandnewatno5parish of ballymoney& derrykeighancauseway family of parishes2nd august 2026 nineteenth sunday of ordinary timekeep your eyes on jesus in this week's gospel, jesus walks across the sea of galilee to his frightened apostles during a storm. peter, full of faith, steps out of the boat to walk towards him — but when he takes his eyes off jesus and looks instead at the wind and waves, he begins to sink. jesus reaches out and saves him, gently asking, "why did you doubt?”life brings storms of its own — worry, illness, family strain, ﬁnancial pressure — that can leave us feeling like we're sinking. this gospel reminds us that jesus is always with us in the midst of them, inviting us to keep our eyes ﬁxed on him rather than on our fears. as st peter later wrote, "cast all your anxieties on him, for he cares about you.” may the lord help us grow in faith and protect us whenever we feel we’re underwater.
